title: Day 48 · Week 6, Day 6 — Myths: get rid of the cat, put down the hair dye, and stay out of the hot bath
summary: The third Myths episode, on the last day of Week 6, and the day the Day 36 promise on hot tubs is paid. Your baby is 7–9 mm at Carnegie stage 15: lens vesicles sealed and going dark with pigment, nasal pits, hand plates, the foramen secundum opening in the upper heart by design, the first gut loop, lobar lung buds and the hemispheres marked out. Myth one, 'get rid of the cat': wrong about the animal, right about the parasite. 91% of US women are susceptible, and the two case-control studies on how pregnant women actually get infected agree — undercooked lamb, beef and game, soil and travel in six European cities (Cook 2000: 'contact with cats was not a risk factor'; 30–63% of infections from meat, 6–17% from soil), and in the US rare lamb aOR 8.4, raw ground beef 6.7, cured meat 2.0, with the one cat finding being three or more kittens at aOR 27.9 (Jones 2009). Why: a cat sheds oocysts for about one week in its life and never again on rechallenge (Davis & Dubey 1995), and oocysts are not infectious until 1–5 days after shedding (CDC), which a daily litter change beats. Myth two, 'no hair dye': mostly a myth. The NHS says most research shows it is safe and 12 weeks is a choice, not a rule; 0.5% of a labelled dark permanent dye was absorbed in eight volunteers (Hueber-Becker 2004); no signal for preterm birth or low birth weight with harsher straighteners (Blackmore-Prince 1999, 525 women); Motherisk calls 3–4 uses a pregnancy not of concern; one positive study for neuroblastoma (McCall 2005, OR 1.6 on a baseline of ~8 per million children a year) against null findings for childhood brain tumours (Holly 2002, 540 cases) and leukaemia (Towle 2017, 20 studies, meta-RR 1.09). Myth three, 'no hot baths': half right. Heat is a teratogen with a 39.0 °C threshold; hot tubs carried RR 2.8 for neural tube defects in 23,491 women (Milunsky 1992), hyperthermia OR 1.92 across 15 studies (Moretti 2005), anencephaly aOR 1.68 and gastroschisis 1.54 in the NBDPS with ≥2-fold odds for long repeated use (Duong 2011), and a possible doubling of miscarriage in 1,063 Kaiser women (Li 2003). But it takes ≥15 min to the neck at 39 °C or ≥10 min at 41 °C to approach the threshold (Harvey 1981), a 40 °C bath leaves pregnant women at a mean 36.9 °C and a 70 °C sauna at 37.6 °C (Ravanelli 2019, 347 women, 20-minute limits), and 98.5% of Finnish mothers use the sauna in pregnancy with one of the lowest CNS-defect rates ever recorded (Saxén 1982). The neural tube sealed around Day 42; the heart and face are still closing. Verdict: bath yes, sauna at 70 °C for 20 minutes yes, hot tub 10 minutes with shoulders out or skip until 12 weeks.
action: Tonight, two things, ten minutes. One: the litter tray is yours until the birth — say it out loud, put it on the chore list, do it daily with a hand wash after (gloves if you like); if there is a kitten, a raw-fed cat or a cat that hunts, the garden gloves go next to it. Two: put a cheap baby bath thermometer in the bathroom and tell her the two numbers: 40 °C (104 °F) is a bath she can stay in; a hot tub is ten minutes with her shoulders out until twelve weeks. If she's been holding off on colouring her hair, tell her what the NHS says and book it.
